missionPremise: A-220 (operator, 2026-09-18, `_decisions/2026-09-18_phase0_closeout_rulings.md`): the program's destructive-write threshold is 0.05, program-wide -- the ENGINE's live number, not the factory's 0.5. P-328's #474, green and HELD at 6b4c3557, made the engine read the factory's 0.5, which would have LOOSENED the engine's live 0.05 tenfold on the writer that retired 92.5 percent of Bastrop (57,704 of 62,394) on 2026-09-15. The row's job is to make the factory carry 0.05 so #474 can land without loosening anything. Read at source: the dispatch's ruling section, and the factory guard's own header (which stated the 0.5 basis it had).

factoryGuard.basis: Williamson's 282,569-of-602,050 legitimate retirement (0.4694, 2026-09-10) sat below it and the two incidents (0.925 Bastrop, 1.000) above it.
factoryGuard.register: DESTRUCTIVE_WRITERS -- wired: publish-retirement (via requireRetirementGate); not wired, with reasons: purge-bastrop-orphans, s6-collision-remediate, vh-collision-remediate, parcel-rail-imports, parcel-cell-rail-resets, dollar-fields-patch.
factoryGuard.scan: test/destructive-write-guard.test.mjs scans src/ so a new destructive statement cannot be missed by omission.

whatExistedAtStart.theBasisHadChangedSince: Since P-327 (#177) `destructive` counts NEW retirements only; rows already retired are re-retirements, reported and never added to the share. P-327's census (`_inbox/2026-09-18_p327-retirement-gate-roll_census.json`, staging, read 2026-09-18T12:56:20Z) reads ZERO new retirements in all six counties, and Williamson's 282,569 R-keyspace rows now read as re-retirements (282,570 total re-retirements, destructive 0, share 0). So the 0.4694 that set 0.5 no longer enters the share at all.

engineSide.asItStoodOnTheBranch: carried the factory's 0.5 pinned by a commit SHA and stated plainly what that cost; the engine's own guards were already 0.05 (MAX_ORPHAN_SHARE, MAX_REACTIVATION_SHARE, live since P-213/P-275).
engineSide.divergenceCheck: packages/engine-core/scripts/check-destructive-write-share-divergence.mjs compares the two offline, and with a local clone re-derives the factory's literals.

whatExistedAtStart.whyOnlyOneDirectionIsEnforceable: hauska-factory is PRIVATE (GitHub API and raw.githubusercontent.com answer 404 for it; `npm view hauska-factory` is E404) and hauska-engine is public. So only the factory's CI can read the other side. P-328's check on the engine side stays as a local/seat re-derivation; the enforceable cross-repo direction is the factory-side job this row builds.

predictedVerdictsAt005.source: _inbox/2026-09-18_p327-retirement-gate-roll_census.json (staging, read 2026-09-18T12:56:20Z; instrument scripts/p327-retirement-census.mjs; six counties; destructiveRule new-retirements-only).
predictedVerdictsAt005.countingRule: destructive = NEW retirements (rows already retired are re-retirements and never enter the share; P-327 #177); share = destructive / population; verdict = the gate's own promoted/refused outcome.
predictedVerdictsAt005.predictedGateSchedulerVerdictAt005: PASS for all six: destructive 0 on every county, so the share is 0 and no authorisation is required. Williamson's 282,570 re-retirements are REPORTED and never enter the share (P-327), which is exactly why 0.05 refuses nothing healthy.
predictedVerdictsAt005.predictedPublishVerdictAt005: No publish step refuses for blast radius: every county's retirement step is either zero-retirement or all-re-retirement. The refusal band 0.05 < share <= 0.5 -- which 0.5 left open -- now REFUSES unauthorised, and that band is where a mass FALSE retirement would land. The Bastrop shape (0.925) refused under 0.5 and refuses under 0.05.
predictedVerdictsAt005.whatChangedVersusAPredictionAt05: No county's verdict changes: at 0.5 the six census verdicts were already pass and they are still pass. What changed is the WIDTH of the refusal: the 5-to-50 percent band is no longer an unauthorised pass on the writer that emptied Bastrop. A legitimately large retirement (the old 0.4694 shape, or a real one larger than 5 percent) must now go through the existing population-bound authorisation (DESTRUCTIVE_WRITE_AUTHORISATION / the guard's token), which is stated in both headers.
